scope: Responsive boundaries, shared layout/spacing names and values, Stack family defaults; partial inventory approval only

decisions.answer: It should probably work exactly how it works with native CSS responsive definitions, no?I think we should just match  chakra
decisions.decision: Match Chakra's range meaning: include lower named threshold, exclude upper named threshold. Express exact bounds with native CSS comparisons rather than automatically copying Chakra's 0.04px subtraction. mediumToLarge covers medium and expanded, ending when large begins.

Spacing properties accept theme spacing values and explicit valid CSS lengths/expressions. Literal values are deliberate overrides and are not automatically rescaled by density. C-SPACE-02 settles numbered token keys; exact supported keys and per-property CSS grammar remain inventory work.

Use numbered spacing token keys. Values identify theme entries rather than pixel counts; raw CSS lengths are explicitly unit-qualified where CSS requires units. Component sizes retain their separate named-word vocabulary. Exact supported keys/default values still require token specification.
Focused shared layout properties use full CSS names and logical inline/block directions. JavaScript uses camelCase and HTML uses kebab-case. No duplicate Chakra shorthand aliases.
Stack, HStack and VStack default gap to house spacing token 2, currently 8px. Authors can override gap, including 0. Token values respond to theme/density rules.

HStack and VStack retain horizontal/vertical direction respectively in their component interfaces. Use general Stack when direction changes responsively. This does not claim CSS cannot override author styling.
